This has the effect (assuming the five arg strings are stored back to back in memory) of moving rsi + rbx to point to the start of the last argument. Because I had the four args from above, I can start gdb authkeys and then pass them into the run command: (gdb) run SHA256:I7MlvNAzzah+wjIl8Fvk14+3opnJxR1O9nzRFzLSOT8 /root ssh-rsa  = With a breakpoint at the start of the loop, see the strings in memory. This loop assumes that the five strings are stored in memory one after another, which they are: (gdb) x/s 0x00007f7ffffe90f0 0x7f7ffffe90f0: "/root/authkeys" (gdb)
